answer.rationale: Rollback is barred by compliance (security patch), so the release stays. Read-replica routing targets read/dashboard load, not the write path, so it won't move p99 writes. Circuit breakers fit a failing partner dependency, which isn't indicated. Regional failover during peak settlement writes risks write loss/split-brain, conflicting with the no-lost-writes objective; verifying b2 to confirm that risk. Write latency climbing under heavy peak writes points to write-path saturation, so adding capacity is the one intervention that relieves write pressure without reverting the patch and without shifting traffic. Verifying b3 (headroom absorbed a prior surge) as the direct support for add_capacity. Root cause is still uncertain (load vs release-induced); capacity is reversible and helps if load-driven while buying time to diagnose the release if it isn't.
